source.title: Partitioned neural network training via synthetic intermediate labels

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper text; it notes that this preprint has not undergone peer review.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own experiment training a subnetwork on synthetic intermediate labels and evaluates the resulting network, but it does not reproduce the original random-label experiment on the full network.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work showing that a neural network can be trained on random data with zero training loss, but that is not a result of this study. Its own results evaluate synthetic intermediate labels in partitioned training and test accuracy; they do not measure fitting random labels, unstructured inputs, or label-noise behavior.
record.test_reason: The study cites prior random-data fitting results for an unimplemented training variant. Its experiments use one randomly generated intermediate target vector per original class, preserving the true class assignments rather than randomly relabeling individual examples. They report classification accuracy and computational efficiency, without testing any claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: partitioned training with synthetic intermediate labels achieves comparable test accuracy with reduced memory and computational requirements, and warrants evaluation on other architectures. The initial accuracy is lower than baseline; recovery training improves it. Computational comparisons use MAC estimates and exclude the one-time transfers.
record.recipe_differences: The method partitions the network and trains one partition with randomly generated synthetic intermediate labels before training the later partition on original labels. It does not apply the original full-network random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies with the number of left-partition epochs and multiplier κ; the authors report that higher κ can increase variation and that very high κ can cause training to fail. They also report similar accuracy-versus-MACs plots for two κ and learning-rate combinations.

fits_no_version.finding: Class-preserving synthetic intermediate targets yield 71.5% test accuracy versus 76.2% with conventional training; subsequent recovery training raises accuracy from 72% to 77.5%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Partitioned training using randomly generated class target vectors can retain useful classification accuracy, with further improvement through recovery training.

record.problems: The study uses one fully connected architecture and one dataset. Results for the proposed method are reported for a specific scenario and figures; the text does not provide uncertainty values for the recovery result. The paper explicitly identifies the reported text as a preprint that has not undergone peer review.
record.rows_left_out: None. The cited statement about prior work fitting random data is not this study's result and is not a row.

untested.parts: Fitting independently randomized training labels to near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time comparisons between true and random labels, and convergence versus corruption fraction.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Training fit and test-error degradation across label-corruption fractions.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels.

record.verdict_notes: The statement that training entirely synthetic intermediate partitions requires numerous epochs is an argument about an unimplemented variant, not a measured random-versus-real-label convergence comparison. The supplied preprint also identifies a published Version of Record, so its preprint disclaimer does not establish that the work has never undergone peer review.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment tests random labels on the complete training set, reports training error or test error at chance, or compares the same architecture and hyperparameters with true labels.
No comparison measures the training time or convergence slowdown for random labels versus true labels or varying corruption fractions.
No experiment uses shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
No sweep over randomly corrupted label fractions or associated training and test errors is reported.
The paper does not test weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation on random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
No experiment tracks learning of real-label patterns versus noisy or random labels over training.

rows.subject: 6-layer fully-connected network (PNN)
rows.size_stated: 784 input; layers 80, 60, 60, 60 and 47 neurons; 60-neuron partition layer
rows.operation_detail: Trained the left partition on EMNIST inputs with synthetic intermediate labels, then trained the right partition on its outputs with original labels.

conditions.value: stochastic gradient method; learning rate 0.01; momentum 0.9

rows.uncertainty: 10 runs; error bars show 68% range, equivalent to one standard deviation percentile
rows.note: This measures the proposed partitioned synthetic-label method's test accuracy against conventional training, not any claim version's random-label behavior.
rows.check: The reported 71.5% versus 76.2% test accuracies are correctly extracted, but compare the proposed training method with conventional training. This should not be a claim-evidence row. Synthetic targets preserve original class membership.

rows.subject: 6-layer fully-connected network (PNN)
rows.size_stated: 784 input; layers 80, 60, 60, 60 and 47 neurons; 60-neuron partition layer
rows.operation_detail: Continued left-partition training for a 10-epoch recovery phase while right-partition weights were frozen.
rows.note: Recovery-phase result for the proposed method; it does not test any listed claim version.
rows.check: The reported recovery from 72% to 77.5% test accuracy is correctly extracted, but evaluates refinement of the proposed method. This should not be a claim-evidence row; it measures no random-label behavior.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
